classification.difficultyReason: Calculate interior angles of adjoining regular polygons and use angles at a point.

content.prompt: Work out the value of the pronumeral, given that these are regular polygons.

spec.description: A square left of a regular hexagon, sharing one vertical side; all unique edges have one equality tick. The lower exterior gap is marked a. Ordinary source grey strokes are reconstructed in house black; no shading.
spec.mathematics: The square interior angle is 90 degrees and the regular hexagon interior angle is 120 degrees. The remaining angle at the shared lower vertex is 150 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the unknown a appears in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Each interior angle of the regular hexagon is
$$\begin{aligned}I&=\frac{180(6-2)}{6}\\I&=120^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
Angles at a point sum to $360^\circ$:
$$\begin{aligned}a+90^\circ+120^\circ&=360^\circ\\a&=150^\circ.\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Regular pentagon left of a regular hexagon, sharing a sloping side. All unique edges have one equality tick. The upper exterior gap is marked b. Ordinary grey source strokes become house black; no shading.
spec.mathematics: Regular pentagon and hexagon interior angles are 108 degrees and 120 degrees. Their upper shared vertex has a remaining gap of 132 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only b is shown in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Each interior angle of the regular pentagon is
$$\begin{aligned}I_5&=\frac{180(5-2)}{5}\\I_5&=108^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
Each interior angle of the regular hexagon is
$$\begin{aligned}I_6&=\frac{180(6-2)}{6}\\I_6&=120^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
Angles at a point sum to $360^\circ$:
$$\begin{aligned}b+108^\circ+120^\circ&=360^\circ\\b&=132^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
